I just got one of those trays last weekend, and started some 12 kinds of seeds in them - tomatoes, kale, squash, cucumber and bush-beans. Many of them sprouted already.

My first batch of seedlings (started in re-used old six-pack starter trays) got wicked mold and fungus gnat issues. I had made the rookie mistake of using compost in my seed starting mix. That plus growing them indoors was great for mold, not so much for the seeds. So I re-started in the jiffy tray using plain peat-moss and vermiculite this time.

It's definitely a mistake most beginners make (myself included). Once you factor in the lack of direct sun and stale air, mold makes too much sense. Dampening is a bitch.

I know peat moss is not a sustainable resource, but it's cheap and sterilized. I've heard good things about coconut choir, but I also hear it's pricier.

I usually tend to prefer coco-coir myself, but this time I didn't have any on hand. So I just went with the peat that I already had, since it was only for the tiny cells in a seed starter.

I have also mixed in a bunch of powdered cinnamon in the starter mix, since I heard it is a natural fungicide.
